items.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998
items.q: I’m commissioned now and then by the Carnegie Hall Jazz Band under the direction of Jon Faddis to write an arrangement for a presentation they do at Carnegie Hall or somewhere

ctx.x: Well I’m sure we’ll talk about that quite a bit because you said some interesting things about that earlier in the jazz history class. Do you get most of your income, is it kind of divided between performing and writing?

Right now it’s divided between performing and publishing. And the writing is a minimal part of it, the actual writing. For instance, I’m commissioned now and then by the Carnegie Hall Jazz Band under the direction of Jon Faddis to write an arrangement for a presentation they do at Carnegie Hall or somewhere, and that will consist of one or two arrangements at a time. And then there’ll be no more writing, actual writing for pay, for © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

another few months or a few weeks. I’m doing a lot of writing that’s for myself, for my three groups, the Non-Electric Company Quartet, the 10-piece dance band called Swing Plus, and the big band called The Loud Minority. But all that, I have to do that on my own time. But the one growing part of my business so to speak is publishing, especially publishing the charts that were done during the Basie era, from 1953 to 1964, and the so- called “Basie heritage era” between 1986 and 1995. items.q: Then you have the Carnegie Hall band under the direction of Jon Faddis... these are perpetuating different styles... and they’re sort of repertory orchestras.

ctx.x: Yeah, I think most of those guys have individual careers that they’re pursuing, you know.

Then you have the Carnegie Hall band under the direction of Jon Faddis, the Lincoln Center Orchestra under the direction of Wynton Marsalis, these are perpetuating different © Fillius Jazz Archive -13-
styles, like from Jelly Roll Morton to Louis Armstrong to Fats Waller to Duke Ellington, etcetera, etcetera, Basie, and they’re sort of repertory orchestras.
